title: Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the tip-heaps at Achadh dhomhain
summary: Before selling his house's last share in An Sloc Mòr, Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the spoil-heaps above Achadh dhomhain with his clerk, ground his family has held a right to for four generations and never before had reason to stand on.

title: Comhairle nam Mèinnean buys An Sloc Mòr's last private share
summary: Comhairle nam Mèinnean takes Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's remaining share in An Sloc Mòr's spoil and quarry-rights at a price haggled down only a little from the house's own asking, glad to hold the whole of An Sloc Mòr in its own hand at last.

title: The first Mac Ùisdein hull takes shape at Ros dhomhain
summary: The first of three dubhan hulls bought with An Sloc Mòr's price is laid down at Ros dhomhain, a coastal trader with her tank amidships and her old grate left in for wood as well, should it ever come to that.

title: A bus line reaches Cathair mhòr
summary: A second dubhan bus line opens between the capital and Cathair mhòr, Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's own town, carrying passengers the eleven miles in under an hour where the old coach took the better part of a morning.

title: The coal caste holds its tongue
summary: The old coal-holding families of the capital say nothing that anyone writes down of the bus, the hired car or the trade turning wholly to dubhan; those with a seam still paying hold their peace because it pays, and those whose seams are spent do quietly, each in its own season, what Taigh Mhic Ùisdein has already done.

title: The patrol boats of Ros dhomhain outrun the raiders
summary: The refitted patrol boats at Ros dhomhain run down two raider hulks in a single month, a speed the harbour's own clerks say the coal-fired fleet never had, and bring both hulks into the harbour wall under tow.

title: The raiders' trial at Cùirt na Mara
summary: Eleven raiders taken off Ros dhomhain stand before Cùirt na Mara; eight Dia-thìrich are sent to the quarries at Achadh dhomhain and three Tuathaich, among them a boy of sixteen, are told they are free to find their own way north.

title: Peigi nic Ascaill reads Riaghailt na Cairte
summary: Peigi nic Ascaill reads the grant chartering Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail and finds, near its foot, the clause fixing the guild's rolls to Dia-thìrich alone. She argues against the clause with Comann nan Sciobairean before the grant is confirmed, and is not heard.

title: Twelve masters sworn to Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail
summary: Twelve masters, Peigi nic Ascaill among the first six called, swear Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' oath at the southern Seann Skell under a clerk of An t-Ionmhas and a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, while the Tuathaich fitters who trained beside them stand outside the roll being read.

title: Peigi nic Ascaill pays Joe Ashby a month over
summary: The evening of the chartering, Peigi nic Ascaill brings Joe Ashby a month's wage over what is owed him and the two other Tuathaich fitters let go with him, and cannot bring herself to come further than his own doorstep to give it.

title: Joe Ashby fits Jean Fisher's boat
summary: Back at Caol mhòr, Joe Ashby fits his first engine outside any guild, to the fishing boat of a widow named Jean Fisher, taking payment half in coin and half in fish.

title: The guild's letter pinned above Joe's bench
summary: Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' court at Seann Skell writes north warning any who fit an engine without the guild's leave that they do so without its protection. Joe Ashby pins the letter above his bench at Caol mhòr rather than burn it.

title: Tional nan Tuathach votes to take up the new fuel
summary: Tional nan Tuathach, under Martha Greaves, votes eleven towns to five that the north shall take up the dubhan fuel it already burns in half its lamps, settling in its own minute what has for two summers simply happened around it.

title: Ruth Calder speaks and the five towns walk out
summary: Ruth Calder, sent to Tional nan Tuathach that year in her dying father's stead, speaks for the western pit towns' right to cut their own coal as long as the seams allow, and leads the five towns' delegates out of the hall before the vote is entered in the book.

title: Martha Greaves keeps the granaries open to all five towns
summary: Asked whether the walk-out closes Tional nan Tuathach's granaries to the western towns, Martha Greaves answers that a hungry household is a hungry household whatever its delegate voted, and the question is not put to her again that year.

title: Bus and tacsaidh at the bridge
summary: At the foot of the bridge in Cathair dhearg the dubhan buses load for Inis mhòr and Cathair mhòr and the hired cars wait for fares; the town calls them by the humans' names, bus and tacsaidh, and nobody coins others.

title: The guild's banner blessed at Seann Skell
summary: At the chartering of Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail in the works' long shed a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail blesses the guild's new banner, a black swan on grey, and twelve masters are sworn.

title: Abel Fowler mends a threshing engine at Muileann bheag
summary: One of the fitters let go from the southern works under Riaghailt na Cairte is taken on at Muileann bheag, on the word of the lighthouse keeper, to mend a threshing engine none of the district's smiths will touch.

title: An Sloc Mòr's pumps run on dubhan
summary: The engine-house at An Sloc Mòr changes its pumps from coal to dubhan, Comhairle nam Mèinnean finding it cheaper to buy the fuel than to burn its own coal.

title: A bus to the springs of Muileann ruadh
summary: A bus of Cathair dhearg begins to run twice weekly to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh, and the custodians of the bath-house find their benches full of townsfolk who are not sick.

title: Cnoc bhàn's boats keep the pirate watch
summary: In the year the raiders are taken off Ros dhomhain, the boats of Cnoc bhàn keep watch in turns on the pirate waters and twice put out to warn the fishing fleet in from the north-east.
